name: FORM4 — SEC Form 4 insider-buy watchlist
what_it_is: A nightly EDGAR crawler, not a strategy. It walks the SEC daily index after 22:10 ET,
parses every Form 4, keeps open-market insider BUYS over $50,000, and posts up to 15 of
them to Discord as a watchlist. It places no orders and holds no positions. Another bot
(picks_trader) decides what to do with the names.
why_there_is_no_genome: There is no entry rule made of price. The input is an SEC filing feed and the output is a
list of names; there is no moving average, no RSI, no lookback and no valuation band
anywhere in the file. Seven genes written here would be seven numbers invented so a
backtest could run, and the backtest would then be measuring the numbers I invented.
The court's 'no readable genome' refusal is the correct ruling on this bot.
why_it_cannot_run_in_the_village: Its entire input is https://www.sec.gov — the court refuses network imports, and rightly.
A scanner wired up here could only ever publish silence.

real_constants.note_on_request_gap: ~8 req/s, under SEC's 10 req/s limit. Two instances would breach it — which is why FIVEWAY deliberately does not start a second copy.

verdict_already_measured.headline: The insider signal is real, it is priced overnight, and retail cannot get in front of it.
verdict_already_measured.sample: SEC quarterly Form 3/4/5 datasets — 974,435 transactions, 31,456 buy events, 4,310 tickers, 2023-01..2026-03
verdict_already_measured.what_is_left_after_the_gap: +0.141% over the next 21 days — 83% of the return is gone before you can trade
verdict_already_measured.filing_times: 82.5% of 2,949 sampled acceptance timestamps land AFTER the close; only 12.2% during market hours
verdict_already_measured.median_abnormal_return: NEGATIVE at every horizon tested (1/5/10/21/63d); the positive mean is a few big winners
verdict_already_measured.placebo: same tickers, random dates — within noise of the real signal
verdict_already_measured.data_check: 10 random rows traced back to the original Form 4 XML on EDGAR: 10/10 exact on ticker, shares and price

what_the_village_could_still_do: Nothing about the signal — that question already has a better-powered answer than a
village replay could produce. What is worth reading is the file itself: rate limiting,
the $1B/$5,000-per-share sanity traps, and the deliberate absence of a webhook fallback.
